sentences.text: Ctenosauriscus was an extinct archosaur known for a prominent sail running along its back. This structure consisted of elongated bony projections extending from the vertebrae in the neck and back regions.
This creature ranks among the earliest known members of the archosaur group, sharing that distinction with species from Russia and China.
The primary specimen was unearthed in early 1871 at a site called Bremke dell, located near Göttingen in Germany.
Friedrich von Huene first named the animal in 1902, but scientists later changed the genus name in 1964 to avoid confusion with an existing lizard.
A comprehensive re-examination of the fossil material was published by a group of six researchers in 2011.
One theory from 1998 suggested the animal walked on two legs and used its sail to manage physical stress during movement.
However, a 2011 analysis argued against this idea, noting that the spine's structure would require impossible muscle attachments to the knee joint.
Further research indicates the sail's mass would have shifted the body's balance forward, likely preventing upright walking.
Evidence suggests the animal may have hunted xiphosurans, which are horseshoe crabs found in the same geological layer.
The species belongs to the family Ctenosauriscidae and is classified within the reptile class.
B. Krebs later reclassified the animal as an archosaur by comparing it to the pseudosuchian Hypselorhachis from Tanzania.
Ctenosauriscus lived during the latest Olenekian stage of the Early Triassic, roughly 247.5 to 247.2 million years ago.
Its environment was an arid floodplain featuring dry, salt-flat-like areas mixed with wetter zones similar to modern swamps.
